# What we have, and what a package has to be

## Eleven packages, ten registered, two empty repos

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- 22 repositories. 11 hold a Julia package, 10 of those are in General.
  `ScoringRules.jl` is not registered
- Six distribution packages, one fitting protocol, one Turing layer, one
  scoring port, one package kit, one automatic differentiation toolbox
- `GenerationTime.jl` and `ReproductionNumber.jl` were created in
  February and have never been pushed to
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- The documentation site lists four of the eleven. The tutorials site is
  one page. The R interface prototype is three months stale and targets
  a package name that no longer exists

::: {.callout-note}
The abstract for this talk says we have `CensoredDistributions.jl` and an
R prototype. It is ten packages behind, and the website is behind that.
:::

::: {.attribution}
`CensoredDistributions.jl` is the 14:45 talk in this room. What you build
with all of it is the 16:45 talk.
:::
:::
::::

## A rigid template, not a modular one

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Most Julia templates are modular and you pick the parts you want.
  Ours overwrites, and a scheduled job re-applies it
- `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` writes 76 files into a package. Most are
  force-managed, so a package cannot drift away from the standard
- 20 workflow callers and one composite action, into 23 reusable
  workflows, each pinned to a commit SHA held in one file
- JuliaFormatter is pinned in one place that feeds the pre-commit hook,
  the isolated formatter test and the CI input together
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-important}
Managed files carry a header saying "MANAGED by
EpiAwarePackageTools.scaffold — do not edit by hand".
:::

- Ten of the eleven packages are on it. The exception is the package the
  tooling was extracted from, and there is an issue open about that
- Uniformity is the point. An agent that has learned one repository has
  learned all of them
:::
::::

## The style guide is a failing test

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
const BANNED_README_WORDS = [
    "comprehensive", "cornerstone",
    "facilitate", "foster",
    "framework", "harness",
    "landscape", "leverage",
    "novel", "pivotal",
    "practitioner", "robust",
    "streamline", "synergy",
    # ... 20 in total
]
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Nine quality checks run in every package: Aqua, ExplicitImports,
  import centralisation, docstring format, README sections, doctests,
  formatting, JET, extension ambiguities
- README sections are named and ordered, and a managed block of them is
  re-rendered on every sync
- JET and the formatter run in their own environments so the pinned
  version cannot drift with the test environment

::: {.callout-note}
A guideline gets ignored. A failing test does not.
:::
:::
